title: Java News Roundup: GraalVM, Jakarta Data, JNoSQL, Azul Payara, WildFly, Quarkus, Atmosphere
gist: A weekly Java ecosystem roundup shows agentic-AI plumbing now spreading into mainstream enterprise Java infrastructure: Azul Payara ships an initial Jakarta Agentic AI spec implementation, Open Liberty adds MCP server support, and Quarkus Flow bakes in LangChain4j orchestration, alongside routine GraalVM, WildFly and security-hardening releases.

themes.theme: Agentic AI standardizing inside Jakarta EE app servers

insights.claim: Azul Payara 7.3.0 (August 2026 edition, spanning its Community, Enterprise 6, and Enterprise 5 editions) introduces the initial implementation of the Jakarta Agentic AI specification, bringing a formal agentic-AI standard into a mainstream Jakarta EE application server.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Enterprise Java vendors are moving agentic AI from bolt-on libraries to a standardized platform specification, which lowers switching costs for enterprises building agents on established app-server stacks rather than newer AI-native frameworks.
insights.quote: This release also introduces the initial implementation of the Jakarta Agentic AI specification.

insights.claim: Open Liberty's beta 26.0.0.9 release adds support for the MCP Java API (org.mcpjava:mcp-server-api:1.0.0) in its mcpServer-1.0 feature, letting IBM's Jakarta EE runtime host Model Context Protocol servers natively.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: MCP support landing directly in enterprise Java runtimes signals MCP is becoming a default integration layer for connecting enterprise Java backends to LLM agents, relevant to any vendor building MCP tooling or competing app-server platforms.
insights.quote: support for the MCP Java API (org.mcpjava:mcp-server-api:1.0.0) in the mcpServer-1.0 feature

insights.claim: Quarkus released version 1.0.0 of Quarkus Flow, a new extension implementing the Open Workflow Specification with a Java DSL definable via YAML or Java code, built-in Agentic AI orchestration via LangChain4j, and cloud-event emit/consume support.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Red Hat's Quarkus is packaging agent orchestration as a first-class workflow product rather than leaving it to third-party frameworks, competing directly with standalone agent-orchestration tooling for enterprise Java shops.
insights.quote: New features include: a Java DSL that can define workflows via YAML or directly in Java code; Agentic AI orchestration with LangChain4j; and the ability to emit and consume cloud events.

insights.claim: Atmosphere 4, described as a real-time engine for AI agents on the JVM, shipped two maintenance releases in one week (4.0.68 and 4.0.69) adding a portable AI agent component and workspace-scoped configuration via a new configureForAgent() method.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: A fast release cadence on a JVM-native AI-agent real-time engine suggests active niche competition for agent-runtime infrastructure below the app-server layer, worth tracking for smaller infra vendors gaining traction in the agentic-AI stack.
insights.quote: The release of Atmosphere 4, a real-time engine for AI agents on the JVM, now includes a portable AI agent component.

themes.theme: Security hardening across the Java stack

insights.claim: JEP 542 (PEM Encodings of Cryptographic Objects) has been targeted for JDK 28 after three rounds of preview across JDK 25 through 27, finalizing an API for converting cryptographic keys, certificates, and revocation lists to and from PEM text format.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Standardized PEM handling in core Java reduces reliance on third-party crypto libraries for certificate/key interoperability, a modest but real maturation signal for enterprise Java security tooling.

insights.claim: WildFly 41.0.1 upgraded to the latest Apache CXF version to support blocking of decoupled destinations as a mitigation against Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks, alongside an updated serialization filter deny list per JEP 290.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Continued SSRF and deserialization hardening in a major open-source Java app server is relevant to enterprise security posture and patch-cycle planning for WildFly-based deployments.

insights.claim: Quarkus 3.39.0 added support for post-quantum cryptography in its TLS Certificate Registry extension while reversing a prior decision to enable reflection-free Jackson serializers by default, citing ongoing stability issues despite improvements.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Post-quantum TLS support arriving in a mainstream Java framework is an early adoption data point for PQC readiness among enterprise middleware vendors; the Jackson reversal is a reminder that performance-oriented defaults still carry real production risk.
